class.name: BaristaScript
class.brief_description: A non-executable BaristaScript source resource with static validation.
class.description: Godot loads [code].barista[/code] files as this [Script] resource through [BaristaScriptResourceLoader]. The source text is preserved and can be checked with [method is_valid]. A successful check means the current parser and semantic analyzer accept the source; it does not make the script executable. Use Godot's resource API from a host language such as GDScript: [codeblock lang=gdscript] var script := ResourceLoader.load("res://example.barista") as BaristaScript if script != null: print(script.source_code) print(script.is_valid()) assert(not script.can_instantiate()) [/codeblock] [method Script.can_instantiate] always returns [code]false[/code]. Runtime and placeholder instances, exported properties, script methods and signals, RPC behavior, and execution are not implemented. Reflection lists for script-defined members are empty even when static analysis succeeds. [method Script.reload] currently returns [constant OK] without compiling or refreshing the source from disk; changing [member Script.source_code] only replaces the stored text. Global declaration metadata is available to the editor for supported named declarations. It is resolved separately from full semantic validity, so an editor-visible global name does not prove that [method is_valid] will succeed. Documentation for declarations inside [code].barista[/code] files is not generated; the help here describes the extension API itself.

method.name: get_build_info
method.description: Returns a fresh dictionary describing the compiled extension library loaded by this process. This read-only instance method is available in ordinary debug and release builds. It does not inspect the current checkout, validate source, or enable script execution. Editing the returned dictionary does not change subsequent results. Schema [code]1[/code] contains [code]schema[/code], [code]extension_version[/code], [code]config_sha256[/code], [code]godot_api[/code], and [code]godot_runtime[/code]. The latter is the runtime version selected by the build configuration, not the actual host Godot version; query [method Engine.get_version_info] separately for the running engine. The nested [code]source[/code] dictionary contains [code]revision[/code] and [code]state[/code]. The nested [code]godot_cpp[/code] dictionary contains [code]selected_revision[/code] (the selected Git submodule revision), [code]revision[/code] (the bindings checkout used), and [code]state[/code]. States are [code]clean[/code], [code]dirty[/code], or [code]unknown[/code]; source archives without Git identity report [code]unknown[/code] instead of claiming a clean revision. These values describe the inputs when the library was built, even if the current checkout has since changed. The nested [code]build[/code] dictionary contains [code]platform[/code], [code]architecture[/code], [code]target[/code], [code]precision[/code], and the boolean [code]native_tests[/code]. Use this metadata with the actual host version when reporting a bug: [codeblock lang=gdscript] var script := BaristaScript.new() print(JSON.stringify(script.get_build_info())) print(Engine.get_version_info()) [/codeblock]

method.name: is_valid
method.description: Parses and semantically analyzes the currently stored [member Script.source_code]. Returns [code]true[/code] only when both stages succeed. The resource path supplies the context for resolving dependencies; use [method ResourceLoader.load] to validate a file in its project context. This method does not execute the script and does not return diagnostics. Godot's editor receives error locations and, in debug builds, warnings through [BaristaScriptLanguage]. Loading a file itself does not perform this validation.
